source_text: Nunc tu ede, ubi aequaverit peccato gratiam, ut, quoniam fides tua non capit remedia praelata vulneribus, saltem capiat in angustum non excedentia comparationem redacta; quod si scriptum uspiam reppereris, Paulum tamen ab hac constabit abhorrere sententia; et ut compendio totus Apostoli sensus eluceat, ait: Gratia ex multis delictis in iustificationem [n176] . Multa autem delicta nec secundum te parvuli habent, qui secundum Apostolum nullum habent.
pass_a_gloss: Now you publish where he equaled grace to sin, so that, since your faith does not take remedies preferred to wounds, it may at least take them reduced into a narrow not exceeding comparison; which if you shall have found written anywhere, it will nevertheless stand that Paul shudders away from this sentence; and that the whole sense of the Apostle may shine out by a shortcut, he says: Grace from many offenses into justification. But little children do not even according to you have many offenses, who according to the Apostle have none.

lemmas.lexica: LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Now show where he made grace equal to sin. Since your faith cannot admit remedies ranked above wounds, let it at least admit remedies squeezed down so that they do not exceed the comparison. Even if you found that written somewhere, Paul would still clearly reject such a view. To bring the apostle’s whole meaning to light briefly, he says: ‘Grace is from many offenses to justification’ (Romans 5:16). Even according to you infants do not have many offenses; according to the apostle they have none.

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
